channel.title: AI News Radar - Frontier AI Intel, Social Signals & Tools
channel.description: Real-time panoramic intelligence radar for global frontier AI breakthroughs, verified leader signals, hands-on tutorials, and applied developer tools.

item.title: Meta releases Muse Ember, its smallest and most cost-efficient AI model yet, saying it delivers more intelligence per dollar than Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6 Luna (Russell Brandom/TechCrunch)
item.description: Meta's Superintelligence Lab has released Muse Ember, a lightweight model optimized for high-frequency agent tasks like tool calls, coding, and document parsing. By offering a significantly lower cost of 10 cents per million input tokens, it challenges competitors like Haiku and Luna to capture the market for large-scale, cost-efficient agentic workflows.

item.title: The future of AI hinges on… Jensen Huang’s sex life?
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is under fire following reports of an affair with former reporter Alice Huang. Her company, Megaspeed, made a sudden, massive $4.8 billion purchase of Nvidia chips, raising alarms as intelligence reports suggest she acted as a honeypot for China’s MSS to gain access to sensitive commercial and potentially political communication.

item.title: Uber launches Uber Parking, an in-app parking reservation tool powered by its SpotHero acquisition, in 15 US cities, including Chicago, NYC, and San Francisco (Andrew J. Hawkins/The Verge)
item.description: Uber has integrated SpotHero technology to launch an in-app parking reservation tool across 15 US cities. The feature allows users to search, book, and pay for parking spots, utilizing QR codes or license plate recognition to manage the parking experience directly within the Uber ecosystem.

item.title: Nancy Pelosi’s replacement is ready to regulate AI
item.description: California State Senator Scott Wiener, having won the congressional seat vacated by Nancy Pelosi, has prioritized AI regulation. Citing new reports on recursive self-improvement in AI, he criticized Congress for its slow pace and demanded urgent federal legislation to mitigate existential risks.

item.title: French officials say Iran's Revolutionary Guards were behind the cyberattacks that knocked out commercial refrigerators and freezers across France in October (Reuters)
item.description: French officials have accused the Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps of orchestrating cyberattacks in October that disabled commercial refrigerators and freezers across France. These attacks disrupted retail cold chains, sparking significant concerns regarding the vulnerability of critical national infrastructure.

item.title: Disney bets on Adobe's Firefly to create brand-safe AI models for its entertainment empire
item.description: Disney announced a multi-year partnership with Adobe at the MAX conference, utilizing Adobe's Firefly Foundry to train custom AI models embedded with its core IP. Driven by divisions like Imagineering and ESPN Edge, the project aims to integrate production-ready, brand-safe generative tools into theme park development, film production, and sports content creation.

item.title: Sources: a Commerce Department investigation into Megaspeed for allegedly smuggling Nvidia chips to China was transferred to the DOJ after Nvidia intervened (New York Times)
item.description: Singapore-based Megaspeed is under fire for allegedly smuggling Nvidia's high-end A-series chips into China. Following Nvidia's intervention and cooperation, the Commerce Department has escalated the case to the Department of Justice, signaling a shift from administrative probe to criminal investigation.

item.title: An interview with ex-Shein Executive Chair Donald Tang who insists it was his decision to step down ahead of the troubled IPO, Shein's valuation rout, and more (Patrick Jenkins/Financial Times)
item.description: Former Shein Executive Chair Donald Tang broke his silence on his resignation, insisting it was his personal decision rather than being pushed out. Amid the company's stalled IPO and valuation rout, Tang's move aims to distance himself from the deepening organizational turmoil and market skepticism.

item.title: Trump’s 60 Minutes interview touched on AI safety, threat to arrest an AI exec
item.description: Donald Trump claimed during a televised interview that he once threatened a prominent AI executive with jail time over dangerous activities. He asserted this intimidation forced the executive to change everything, using the anecdote to argue that AI risks are manageable under government oversight.

item.title: Tencent's AI chief says AI bioweapons are coming, but closing off models isn't the answer
item.description: Tencent AI scientist Yao Shunyu warns that AI's potential for bioweapon development, combined with blurred lines between offense and defense, makes neither full open-source nor closed-source models a silver bullet. Citing the Hugging Face incident, he advocates for a nuanced middle ground to balance utility and risk.

item.title: Draft law: the EU's Digital Fairness Act would require companies to let adults disable addictive features and will target AI bots that simulate relationships (Bloomberg)
item.description: The EU is drafting the 'Digital Fairness Act' to crack down on addictive platform designs, mandating that companies provide users with the option to disable such features. The legislation also specifically targets AI chatbots that simulate human relationships to mitigate psychological dependency.

item.title: Hold up — I had a great time talking to the RIAA guy
item.description: Mitch Glazier, CEO of the RIAA, stated that copyright owners, artists, and the public share a growing resentment toward unauthorized AI data scraping. The discussion focused on legal complexities of deepfakes and the urgent need for standardized AI labeling and detection systems on major distribution platforms.

item.description: Risa Heller, the firm’s founder, has built a reputation as a fixer for powerful men facing allegations of sexual misconduct and other personal controversies, according to a 2023 New York Magazine profile. Her past clients and people who have sought her advice include former congressman Anthony Weiner, chef Mario Batali, and writer Jeffrey Toobin. item.title: Spines, which uses AI agents to edit and proofread amateur authors' books, design their covers, and handle the layout, raised $29M in equity and $35M in debt (Assaf Gilead/Globes)
item.description: Digital publishing platform Spines recently secured $29 million in equity and $35 million in debt financing. The company leverages AI agents to assist amateur authors with editing, proofreading, cover design, and layout, reaching an ARR of $50 million.

item.title: Jonathan Kanter is using AI to take on Big Tech
item.description: Former DOJ antitrust chief Jonathan Kanter and his team launched FluxCap. Comprised of former DOJ staffers and Palantir engineers, the company is building AI-powered legal analysis tools to serve as a 'force multiplier' for plaintiffs tackling tech monopolies.

item.title: Sources: Alice Huang and her partner pitched a Southeast Asia data center project to China-based investors in 2025, saying they had "no problem securing GPUs" (Financial Times)
item.description: Alice Huang and her partners were reportedly pitching a data center project in Southeast Asia to investors from China in 2025. They leveraged their connection to Jensen Huang as a selling point, claiming to have 'no problem securing GPUs' through special access.

item.title: Nominal, which builds software to make hardware manufacturing more efficient, raised $240M at a $3B valuation, up from $1B after raising $80M in March (Paayal Zaveri/Bloomberg)
item.description: Nominal Inc., a startup building software to make manufacturing more efficient, has raised $240 million in funding at a $3 billion valuation …

item.title: The Download: empty AI climate claims, and an Nvidia investigation
item.description: At the UN climate conference in Turkey, nations are discussing how to harness AI for climate action. Despite optimistic claims from tech companies about AI's potential, the industry currently lacks concrete actions, with its massive energy footprint actually exacerbating global warming.

item.title: Innovating with AI in the special chemicals industry
item.description: Specialty chemicals manufacturer Lubrizol is building a digital foundation integrating cloud infrastructure and decades of technical data to empower R&D teams with AI-driven hypothesis testing. The initiative aims to combine human scientific judgment with predictive modeling to accelerate innovation and sustainable material development.

item.title: Google ships four TPU variants in one year as it ramps up competition with Nvidia
item.description: Google has launched two new systems in its 8th-gen TPU lineup, TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max, targeting confidential computing and memory-intensive AI workloads. By utilizing a modular packaging approach on existing silicon, Google aims to accelerate hardware deployment cycles to better compete for external cloud customers.

item.title: Google unveils two specialized TPUs, the TPU 8tx, to be paired with AMD CPUs, and TPU 8i Max, a dual-chip package for long-context window tasks, launching 2027 (Dina Bass/Bloomberg)
item.description: Alphabet Inc.'s Google is rolling out a broader array of artificial intelligence chips, aiming to capitalize on its rapid ascent …

item.title: Google unveils two specialized TPUs launching in 2027: the 8tx, to be paired with an AMD CPU, and the 8i Max, a dual-chip package for long-context window tasks (Dina Bass/Bloomberg)
item.description: Google has unveiled two specialized TPU processors slated for 2027. The 8tx is designed for heterogeneous integration with AMD CPUs, while the 8i Max features a dual-chip package specifically optimized for long-context window tasks, aiming to solidify Google's infrastructure advantage.

item.title: Alphabet's Wing plans to invest up to $125M over two years to build a 15,000-square-foot facility in Fort Worth, Texas, to produce tens of thousands of drones (Mark R. Long/Wall Street Journal)
item.description: Alphabet's drone subsidiary Wing plans to invest up to $125 million over two years to construct a 15,000-square-foot production facility in Fort Worth, Texas. This move aims to ramp up manufacturing capabilities to produce tens of thousands of drones, accelerating its commercial expansion in the delivery sector.

item.title: Meta says it is globally expanding Instagram's AI age estimation tech to apply Teen Account protections to teens aged 13 to 17 who misrepresented their age (Jess Weatherbed/The Verge)
item.description: Meta is expanding its AI-powered age estimation technology globally to identify underage users who misrepresented their age by analyzing interaction data and physical cues. This move forces these users into 'Teen Account' restrictions, aiming to mitigate regulatory scrutiny over safety and platform addiction.

item.title: A profile of Alice Huang, a suspected Chinese spy who founded Megaspeed in 2023 and spent years in Jensen Huang's orbit; Megaspeed's Nvidia imports top $4.6B (Mark Anderson/Bloomberg)
item.description: Alice Huang, a mysterious figure formerly close to Nvidia’s leadership, is under scrutiny for founding Megaspeed and allegedly facilitating the export of over $4.6 billion worth of Nvidia chips to restricted territories. The situation highlights deep-seated vulnerabilities in the global AI chip supply chain.

item.title: US voters in Harwood, North Dakota rejected a ballot measure that opposed Applied Digital's $3B data center, set to open in 2027, bucking a nationwide backlash (Miriam Waldvogel/Washington Post)
item.description: Voters in Harwood, North Dakota, rejected a ballot measure intended to block Applied Digital's $3 billion data center project slated for 2027. Despite a growing national backlash against energy-intensive AI infrastructure, the local community opted to prioritize the potential economic and fiscal benefits of the massive project.

item.title: Nvidia espionage scandal weakens Huang's lobby against tighter AI chip export controls
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang acknowledged an affair with a former executive of a Singaporean data center operator, who US intelligence identifies as a suspected Chinese informant. This scandal emerges as the incoming Congress prepares to escalate scrutiny on AI chip smuggling, effectively undermining Huang's lobbying efforts against tighter export controls.

item.title: Amsterdam police arrested between 150 and 200 protesters for trespassing and violence at a Microsoft data center construction site owned by Pure Data Centers (Jowi Morales/Tom's Hardware)
item.description: Amsterdam police arrested 150-200 protesters for trespassing and vandalizing a data center construction site owned by Pure Data Centers. The group opposes the use of fossil fuels by tech giants during energy shortages and plans a wave of protests across Europe.

item.title: Internal EU assessment: Russia's "Operation Overload" opportunistically exploited recent French riots by spreading fabricated videos impersonating Western media (Reuters)
item.description: An internal EU assessment has uncovered a covert operation dubbed 'Operation Overload.' This campaign leveraged recent riots in France by spreading fabricated videos impersonating Western media outlets to fuel social instability.
